title: Ventricular Noncompaction / Ventricular Hypertrabeculation in the Setting of Heterotaxy Syndrome - A Congenital Disorder of Epicardial Origin?
content: Data from animal models show that disrupted embryonic epicardial development can cause ventricular noncompaction/hypertrabeculation (VNC/VHT) and suggest that congenital disorders of visceral left-right patterning (heterotaxy syndrome), particularly bilateral left-sidedness (left atrial isomerism, LAI), may lead to VNC/VHT via embryonic/fetal epicardiopathy. In order to clarify whether the animal model-data fit to humans, we evaluated the prevalence, anatomic associations, and outcomes of VNC/VHT in patients with LAI versus right atrial isomerism (RAI). This retrospective cross-sectional study examined 160 pediatric patients with congenital heart disease and heterotaxy treated at a single center (2000–2023). Patients were assigned to LAI or RAI sub-cohorts; myocardial architecture was determined primarily via rigorous, multi-observer echocardiography. Mid- to long-term survival and freedom from intervention were analyzed by Kaplan–Meier methods. Of 160 patients (median age at diagnosis 1.4 months), 115 (72%) had LAI and 45 (28%) had RAI. VNC/VHT of the morphologic left ventricle was identified in 31 patients (19.3% of the total cohort) and was confined exclusively to LAI (26.9% vs 0% in RAI; p=0.001). Among LAI patients, a strong, statistically significant association was uncovered between VNC/VHT and atrioventricular septal defects (AVSDs), which occurred in 61.3% of VNC/VHT patients compared to 33% without VNC/VHT (p=0.007). Five- and 10-year survival did not differ by VNC/VHT status (p=0.74). However, LAI infants with VNC/VHT underwent first intervention significantly earlier (median 3.3 vs 4.7 months; p=0.035), with 80% requiring a procedure by 12 months versus 66% without VNC/VHT (p=0.04). This study provides the first statistically robust evidence of a specific association between LAI and VNC/VHT and confirm the pathogenetic hypothesis that errors in left-right patterning - specifically bilateral left-sidedness - can lead to VNC/VHT via an embryonic/fetal epicardiopathy. Although long-term mortality is unaffected, VNC/VHT accelerates the need for intervention and warrants intensified surveillance in the first year of life.
